x.intro: Gitega is the second largest city of Burundi and since 2019 the national political capital, as well as the capital of the Gitega Province.

must.d: Opened in 1955, the Burundian National Museum presents exhibits related to Burundian royalty from the early 20th century, archaeologic discoveries, everyday objects from jewelry to pots and spears, and coins from the colonial era.
Catholic cathedral, and the seat of the Gitega Archdiocese.

cities.d: the largest city and longtime capital, situated on the north-eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika

x.around: Taxis are cruising all over the city; you need to negotiate the price with them. Minibuses serving the north of the city arrive and depart at the front of the central market (Marché Central), while those heading south use the parking lot in the back of the market near the Interbank head office. The last mini-buses leave around 22:00 as of 2011.

hidden.d: A nice viewpoint on Bujumbura, 32 east of the city. The road RN1 drive you around 1200 higher than Bujumbura, at 2200. Eat some brochettes “je m’en fout” (means “I don’t care”).
Mausoleum in memory of Burundi's national and independence hero. The place where Burundian Independence Day is celebrated annually on 1 July.

x.intro: Bujumbura is the former capital and largest city of Burundi. It is on the north-eastern shore of Lake Tanganyika, the second deepest lake in the world after Lake Baikal.

must.d: It's not the spot where Stanley said “Dr Livingstone, I presume?”, but it has a gorgeous view of the lake. Livingstone and Stanley passed through the area and carved their names on a large rock.

Small “zoo” and natural history museum. Exhibits include fishes from Lake Tanganyika, birds, seven species of snakes, two chimpanzees called “Kita” and “Joy”, a golden monkey, a leopard called “Jango”, three antelope, two…

x.safe: Bujumbura is a moderately safe city, but common sense should prevail. Walking around during the day should be fine, but at night time (from 18:00) the streets get very dark and you are best off getting a taxi except for very short walks. Day or night there are very few police around. The area near the port feels pretty dodgy day or night.

x.intro: Bururi is a town in the southern region of Burundi and the capital of Bururi Province. It is known for its scenic highlands, rich biodiversity, and cultural heritage.

intro: Burundi is a small country in East Africa, although it has some cultural and geographical ties with Central Africa. It is surrounded by Rwanda, Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Although the country is rich in culture and history, the country has been in a state of instability since gaining independence in the 1960s. Burundi is one of the world's poorest and least developed countries and has a myriad of social, political, and economic problems.

x.around: The best way to explore the forest is on foot, utilizing the walking circuits along botanical lanes and trails. Hiring a local guide is highly recommended to enhance your experience and ensure safety.
x.intro: Bururi Forest National Reserve is a protected area located in southwestern Burundi, covering an expanse of 3,300 hectares (33 km²) of altitude damp forest. Established in 1951 and classified as a wilderness area (IUCN protected area category Ib), it is managed by the Institut National pour l’Environnement et la Conservation de la Nature (INECN). The reserve is a crucial site for biodiversity, featuring a rich variety of flora and fauna.

other.d: . At the apex of the Zaire-Nile, with its 40,000 ha of preserved forests, this the largest completely untouched natural area in Burundi.

x.intro: Kibira National Park (French: Parc national de Kibira) is a vital national park located in northwestern Burundi. Covering approximately 400 km² (150 sq mi) and spanning four provinces, it lies atop the mountains of the Congo-Nile Divide. The park extends from the provincial town of Muramvya to the Rwandan border, where it adjoins Nyungwe National Park.

other.d: Home to Gustave, the infamous man-eating crocodile, Rusizi National Park will be your first visit in Burundi for the simple reason that it is very near the capital city of Bujumbura.

x.intro: Rusizi National Park is located north of Bujumbura in Burundi. It is home to Gustave, the infamous man-eating crocodile.

other.d: The National Park of Ruvubu lies on the banks of the Ruvubu River and is limited by high rise mountains. It was freed from human inhabitants and returned to complete wild life.
